title: mPacket dissection improvements
description:
* Added support for dissecting mPackets with arbitrary preamble length,
  in accordance with IEEE 802.3br-2016
  Changed fpp.preamble type from FT_UINT64 to FT_BYTES

* If the first preamble octet is 0x50: interprets that as padding inserted by capture device due to non-integer preamble length.
  Added fpp.preamble.pad to indicate any alignment padding bits

* Added missing printouts of SMD types
  i.e. SMD-E, SMD-V, SMD-R, SMD-S0, ...

* Added missing printouts of decoded fragment numbers
  i.e. 0, 1, 2, 3

I am not 100% sure this is the true intention for PACK_FLAGS_UNALIGNED_FRAME. It is not exactly well documented.
But I don't know of any other logical purpose this flag could possibly have for mPackets.

> Note: I am not 100% sure this is the true intention for PACK_FLAGS_UNALIGNED_FRAME.

It's an error indication, and probably should be renamed PACK_FLAGS_MISALIGNED_FRAME.

See, for example, [this page of an Ethernet adapter manual](https://manualsdump.com/en/manuals/asante_technologies-asante_maccon_family_ethernet_network_cards_for_the_macintosh/142796/53), in which it lists various error indications, including Frame Alignment Error, which means the frame didn't not end in an 8 bit boundary.

Those flags come from an example given in [the documentation of the flags field of the pcapng Enhanced Packet Block](https://pcapng.github.io/pcapng/draft-tuexen-opsawg-pcapng.html#name-enhanced-packet-block-flags):

> link-layer-dependent errors (Bit 31 = symbol error, Bit 30 = preamble error, Bit 29 = Start Frame Delimiter error, Bit 28 = unaligned frame error, Bit 27 = wrong Inter Frame Gap error, Bit 26 = packet too short error, Bit 25 = packet too long error, Bit 24 = CRC error, other?? are 16 bit enough?).

Currently, we support that flag in DOS Sniffer files; we do *not* yet interpret the link-layer-dependent errors in pcapng files.

Perhaps what *should* be done is, instead, to scan the preamble, a nibble-pair at a time, until a nibble pair unequal to 0x55 is seen.  Once that nibble pair is seen, the length of the preamble is known.

> Frame Alignment Error, which means the frame didn't not end in an 8 bit boundary.

Ok! Then I certainly cannot use it.

> Perhaps what *should* be done is, instead, to scan the preamble, a nibble-pair at a time, until a nibble pair unequal to 0x55 is seen. Once that nibble pair is seen, the length of the preamble is known.

Not sure how you mean?

Let's say this is the data on the wire:

5 5 5 5 D F F F F F F F F F F F F 1 1 1 1

How should it be written to a pcapng file?

Preamble is 5 5 5, SFD is D5, Ethernet destination adr is FFFFFFFFFF


**Option 1: Written directly as-is:**

55 55 FD FF FF FF FF FF 1F 11 1

As you can see, everything is shifted by 4 bits, and there is a single 4 bit nibble remaining on the end.
There would be a lot of bit-shifting to dissect this frame.


**Option 2: The capture device adds 4 bits of padding "p" at the beginning before writing it to pcapng.**

5p 55 D5 FF FF FF FF FF FF 11 11

Now everything is aligned and nice. But how can the dissector recognize that the "p" bits are not actually a part of the frame?
I used PACK_FLAGS_UNALIGNED_FRAME as indication for this, but that is obviously not possible.
Perhaps I could use the "Preamble error" and/or "Start Frame Delimiter" error"?
Let's say the capture device inserts "0" as padding. If there was a zero there on the wire, that would certainly be a preamble error or SFD error. But if no such error is indicated, perhaps the dissector can infer that this "0" is padding?

Or perhaps even simpler: The dissector could ignore the error flags, and just assume that anything which is not "5" in the first byte is padding?

I suppose that would not be strictly IEEE compliant, but I think it could work in practice. The way the Ethernet PHY-layers are specified makes it physically impossible for anything but "5" to be the first bits seen at the reconciliation sublayer.

**Option 3: The capture device chops off bits at the beginning before writing it to pcapng.**

55 D5 FF FF FF FF FF FF 11 11

Now we are losing 4 bits of data. It works, but the dissector has no way of showing the user that the preamble on the wire actually was 4 bits longer.

added 1 commit
  • 4d1b2f9a - mPacket dissection improvements
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/2137/diffs?diff_id=146100617&start_sha=d412ac343d4b76e8701cadce46091ad06478ad75)

I removed the use of PACK_FLAGS_UNALIGNED_FRAME. Now it simply checks if the first byte is 0x50 or not to determine if there are any padding bits or not.

Do you think this approach is reasonable?

Where I work it would be useful to have accurate display of true preamble length for some network troubleshooting purposes.
Preamble reduction is a very common phenomenon on Ethernet today.

But if you believe it would be better to only handle full octets in the wireshark dissector, then we would have to accept that.
changed the description

> Do you think this approach is reasonable?

Yes.

Note that another possibility would be to get another LINKTYPE_ value, for "Ethernet with preamble and SFD/SMD", which would include the preamble length in bits as metadata, with (preamble_length + 7)/8 bytes of preamble following (and with preamble_length%8 low-order bits of zero in the first octet of preamble, if preamble_length is non-zero).

If there are any other interesting pieces of metadata when reception is done below the MAC service point, that could be provided as well.  (Think of it as "radiotap for Ethernet.)

What would the advantage of a new LINKTYPE be?
It would be a second LINKTYPE containing exactly the same IEEE802.3br frames as LINKTYPE_ETHERNET_MPACKET, in exactly the same format.

I do think it could be a good idea to have some metadata exactly describing the preamble length.
But would it not be better to just add new optional metadata bits to the epb_flags, or a new option field to EPB, for the current LINKTYPE_ETHERNET_MPACKET? That way it would be backwards compatible.


There is already a bit of a duplicate: LINKTYPE_NETANALYZER_TRANSPARENT is essentially the same thing as LINKTYPE_ETHERNET_MPACKET.
Adding third LINKTYPE for the same thing sounds like the start of LINKTYPE mess?

> It would be a second LINKTYPE containing exactly the same IEEE802.3br frames as LINKTYPE_ETHERNET_MPACKET, in exactly the same format.

No, it wouldn't.  At minimum, it would contain a preamble length, and might contain other metadata.

> But would it not be better to just add new optional metadata bits to the epb_flags

No.  That would only work with pcapng, not pcap.

> There is already a bit of a duplicate: LINKTYPE_NETANALYZER_TRANSPARENT is essentially the same thing as LINKTYPE_ETHERNET_MPACKET.

"Essentially" does a lot of work here.  That frame also contains metadata, including error flags and other information - including a version field, allowing it to be extended to include additional metadata, so its *not* the same thing as LINKTYPE_ETHERNET_MPACKET.

> Adding third LINKTYPE for the same thing sounds like the start of LINKTYPE mess?

The mess started when LINKTYPE_ETHERNET_MPACKET was added, given that LINKTYPE_NETANALYZER_TRANSPARENT already existed at that point.

And if you want to see a *mess*, look at all the different 802.11 metadata headers.

Perhaps the way to keep the mess from *expanding* is to pick a single "Ethernet plus metadata" header, and use that for all future cases where Ethernet frames plus metadata headers are desired.

> > It would be a second LINKTYPE containing exactly the same IEEE802.3br frames as LINKTYPE_ETHERNET_MPACKET, in exactly the same format.
>
> No, it wouldn't. At minimum, it would contain a preamble length, and might contain other metadata.

Ok, I was under the impression that metadata should be put in the EPB options. Looks like pcapng was designed exactly to allow that kind of extensibility and future-proofing.

> > But would it not be better to just add new optional metadata bits to the epb_flags
>
> No. That would only work with pcapng, not pcap.

But, it would actually *work* fine with pcap.

Lacking the metadata, it would just not have any knowledge about the fractional-byte part of the preamble. That's all. It would still dissect the packet just fine.

Just like pcap dissectors have no knowledge about the "symbol error", "preamble error", "Start Frame Delimiter error", "unaligned frame error", and "wrong Inter Frame Gap error" for mPackets. That is low-level metadata of very similar type as fractional byte preamble.

> > There is already a bit of a duplicate: LINKTYPE_NETANALYZER_TRANSPARENT is essentially the same thing as LINKTYPE_ETHERNET_MPACKET.
>
> "Essentially" does a lot of work here. That frame also contains metadata, including error flags and other information - including a version field, allowing it to be extended to include additional metadata, so its *not* the same thing as LINKTYPE_ETHERNET_MPACKET.

Yes, I am aware. LINKTYPE_NETANALYZER_TRANSPARENT is very much custom-made for a particular propriatary capture device.

> > Adding third LINKTYPE for the same thing sounds like the start of LINKTYPE mess?
>
> The mess started when LINKTYPE_ETHERNET_MPACKET was added, given that LINKTYPE_NETANALYZER_TRANSPARENT already existed at that point.

In some sense, yes.
At least LINKTYPE_ETHERNET_MPACKET refers to a IEEE standard, and does not contain anything proprietary. So I can see some reason there.

> And if you want to see a *mess*, look at all the different 802.11 metadata headers.

I can imagine... I'll have a look :-)

> Perhaps the way to keep the mess from *expanding* is to pick a single "Ethernet plus metadata" header, and use that for all future cases where Ethernet frames plus metadata headers are desired.

It is really difficult to make absolutely sure something is future-proof, unless we can use an extensible format like pcapng.


If we put it like this:
 
Do you agree that support for arbitrary whole-octet length preamble and the addition of the missing text printouts should be committed to LINKTYPE_ETHERNET_MPACKET regardless?
Those changes just improves the dissection, and makes it more IEEE 802.3br-2016 compliant. Without any disadvantages or compatibility issues I can think of.


The only things up for discussion is really how to handle fractional-byte preamble?

Do you think it would be a good idea for me to remove the fractional byte preamble support from this commit, and we could continue that discussion on the mailing list perhaps? Or I could just put it up as a separate commit.

> I was under the impression that metadata should be put in the EPB options

There's metadata and there's metadata.

There's link-layer-independent metadata, such as "hash of the packet contents", "number of packets dropped by the capture mechanism before this packet", "is this really the same packet, at least above the link layer, as this other packet, even though they're on different interfaces", "on which interface queue was this received", "how was this packet classified by some part of the network stack", "here's a note about this packet that somebody who looked at the capture added", etc..

And there's link-layer-*dependent* metadata, such as "on which radio channel was this received", "what PHY was used to transmit it", "does it have an FCS?" (not all link layers *have* an FCS), "how long is the FCS" (not all link layers support negotiating the presence of, and length of, the FCS), "what errors occurred when it was received", etc..

In my experience with libpcap, tcpdump, Wireshark, and capture file formats, I see the former as appropriate for per-packet options in pcapng and the latter as appropriate for a per-link-layer-type metadata header.

> Lacking the metadata, it would just not have any knowledge about the fractional-byte part of the preamble. That's all. It would still dissect the packet just fine.

The only reason I see for it would be if the "what if there were no bits of preamble and an SFD error with an octet of 0x50" problem were an issue.  If not, then the only knowledge needed is "was the preamble not a multiple of 8 bits?", and the answer is "if the first octet is 0x55, it was a multiple of 8 bits, otherwise if it's 0x55 ANDed with a bit mask with a bunch of 1 bits at the top followed by 0 bits, it wasn't a multiple of 8 bits".

> Just like pcap dissectors have no knowledge about {receive errors}

Presumably by "pcap dissectors" you mean "dissectors when they are dissecting packets from a file format that doesn't supply receive error information" - there aren't separate "pcap dissectors" and "pcapng dissectors" (and "DOS sniffer dissectors" and "Windows sniffer dissectors" and...), and there shouldn't be.

> It is really difficult to make absolutely sure something is future-proof, unless we can use an extensible format like pcapng.

Or an extensible *metadata header* like [radiotap](https://www.radiotap.org) or [the 802.15.4 metadata header](https://github.com/jkcko/ieee802.15.4-tap/blob/master/IEEE%20802.15.4%20TAP%20Link%20Type%20Specification.pdf).

> The only things up for discussion is really how to handle fractional-byte preamble?

Yes.  If padding it with zeros suffices to handle it, go with that for now.  If an Ethernettap header is ever proposed, we can consider whether the preamble length is a necessary TLV for it.

> > Lacking the metadata, it would just not have any knowledge about the fractional-byte part of the preamble. That's all. It would still dissect the packet just fine.
>
> The only reason I see for it would be if the "what if there were no bits of preamble and an SFD error with an octet of 0x50" problem were an issue. If not, then the only knowledge needed is "was the preamble not a multiple of 8 bits?", and the answer is "if the first octet is 0x55, it was a multiple of 8 bits, otherwise if it's 0x55 ANDed with a bit mask with a bunch of 1 bits at the top followed by 0 bits, it wasn't a multiple of 8 bits".

Agreed.

I can't think of a situation where this approach would cause problems in practice. The PHY-layers are incapable of sending anything but "5" as the first nibble of preamble to the reconciliation sublayer.

> > The only things up for discussion is really how to handle fractional-byte preamble?
> 
> Yes. If padding it with zeros suffices to handle it, go with that for now. If an Ethernettap header is ever proposed, we can consider whether the preamble length is a necessary TLV for it.

Sounds good.

commits_data.title: mPacket dissection improvements
commits_data.message:
mPacket dissection improvements

* Added support for dissecting mPackets with arbitrary preamble length,
  in accordance with IEEE 802.3br-2016
  Changed fpp.preamble type from FT_UINT64 to FT_BYTES

* Allowed for capture device to signal non-integer preamble length by padding with zero.
  Added fpp.preamble.pad to indicate any alignment padding bits

* Added missing printouts of SMD types
  i.e. SMD-E, SMD-V, SMD-R, SMD-S0, ...

* Added missing printouts of decoded fragment numbers
  i.e. 0, 1, 2, 3
